Cadherin-11 is expressed in the developing eye and optic muscles; abnormal orbital and periocular development is a plausible basis for strabismus, reported in one case.

nodes.description: Cadherin-11 is the type II cadherin switched on as cranial neural crest cells undergo epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition, and it is strongly expressed in human embryonic facial mesenchyme, including palatal and dental mesenchyme and the developing eye and optic muscles. In Xenopus, cadherin-11 activity must be balanced: overexpression blocks neural crest migration, an ectodomain-deleted form causes premature emigration, and a form with disabled EC1 adhesive residues produces non-directional, incomplete migration. Whether TBHS2 variants perturb neural crest migration in human embryos is inferred, not shown.
